entry.title: Fuse Games Details Distributed Development Framework for Star Wars: Galactic Racer
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

Fuse Games CEO Matt Webster has outlined the three-tiered distributed development framework used to build Star Wars: Galactic Racer with a lean core team of approximately 75 people. The production model divides labor across traditional asset outsourcing, external development for self-contained features, and deeply integrated co-development partnerships.

The structure allowed the studio to scale production capacity while maintaining a sustainable core team size, contrasting with traditional AAA structures that rely on massive internal headcounts. Webster detailed how external teams handle discrete components like photo mode while co-developers participate directly in daily stand-ups and shared communication channels as extensions of the core studio.

entry.title: Permit Pending Browser-Based City Simulation Game Released
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | permit.petercai.com | hacker news

Permit Pending is a free, browser-based city simulation game created by Peter Cai where players act as elected mayors rather than omnipotent planners. The gameplay centers on navigating bureaucratic hurdles such as zoning boards, neighborhood opposition, public hearings, and legal appeals.

The underlying economy connects resident incomes, housing costs, and business growth, while players face reelection every four years and manage council votes. The title runs directly in modern web browsers without requiring downloads or accounts, offering an open-ended sandbox experience focused on urban politics and planning constraints.

entry.title: Innersloth Co-Founder Forest Willard Warns Indie Developers of Predatory Publishing Deals
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com

Innersloth co-founder and Outersloth fund overseer Forest Willard has cautioned independent game developers about predatory publishing agreements circulating in the industry. Speaking at the Seattle Loves Indies Creator Expo, Willard stated that he has reviewed term sheets containing abysmal conditions that leave creators with little chance of financial return.

Willard emphasized that while funding limitations prevent his own indie fund from rescuing every studio, the prevalence of exploitative contracts highlights systemic risks in independent game development. His remarks echo similar warnings from other industry leaders regarding unbalanced risk allocation in publisher-developer agreements.

entry.title: Griffin Gaming Partners and Entertainment 360 Launch Production Company Hitpoint Entertainment
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com

Griffin Gaming Partners and Entertainment 360 have launched Hitpoint Entertainment, a joint venture production company focused on adapting video games for film and television. The new studio will identify, develop, and produce adaptations across multiple genres, ranging from action and comedy to romance.

Hitpoint aims to discover and secure video game intellectual property at an early stage, applying a development model traditionally used for books and literary properties in Hollywood. The venture combines Griffin Gaming Partners' expertise in the games industry with Entertainment 360's talent management and production background.

entry.title: Weball Browser Game Lets Players Roll Up Websites Like Katamari
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | funwithcomputervision.com | hacker news

Weball is a browser-based game created by developer Alan that turns ordinary web pages into interactive levels inspired by Katamari Damacy. Players roll a ball across websites, collecting DOM elements and growing larger as they navigate from link to link across the internet.

Because pages load without executing their JavaScript, sites that rely heavily on client-side rendering can appear sparse during gameplay. The project gained traction online following its release, offering a novel way to explore and interact with web content using physics-based rolling mechanics.

entry.title: RocketWerkz and Ahwoo Release Open-Source C# Framework BRUTAL
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

Ahwoo and RocketWerkz have released their C# game development framework, BRUTAL, as open source. The framework combines C# and .NET with C++ libraries and low-level graphics access, giving developers an alternative foundation to build custom tools and game engines without relying on third-party software.

BRUTAL is free for commercial use under an attribution-only license and has been used in projects like Kitten Space Agency and Ludeon Studios' Rimworld. While adoption requires a willingness to work with low-level code, the creators note that large language models can assist developers in querying structured documentation for the framework.

entry.title: Digital Sun Delays ReVamp Public Playtest Due to AI Cloning Concerns
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

Digital Sun Games has postponed the planned public Steam playtest for its upcoming tower-defense action game ReVamp, citing concerns that generative AI tools could be used to reverse-engineer and clone the game before its release. Instead of a broad public build, the studio will host a restricted playtest through its Discord server beginning October 29.

The decision highlights a growing trend among indie developers scaling back public demos and playtests amid rising instances of copycats using advanced language models to decompile and replicate game mechanics. This emerging threat exposes friction between traditional indie marketing strategies, which rely heavily on early public exposure, and the new vulnerabilities introduced by rapid AI code-generation capabilities.

entry.title: Apple App Store Head Discusses Gaming Strategy and Indie Games Week
entry.content:
Techmeme | polygon.com

Carson Oliver, Apple's new head of App Store Worldwide, discussed the company's evolving gaming strategy during an interview following the launch of "Indie Games Week," an initiative featuring several indie titles and the announcement of a mobile version of No Man's Sky. Oliver emphasized Apple's goal to position the App Store as a major destination for premium indie games, supported by investments in hardware like the A20 Pro chip and developer tools such as the Game Porting Toolkit 4.

The strategy seeks to bridge the gap between mobile and console gaming by leveraging improved device performance and enhanced discoverability tools like "Creative Assets." While Apple Arcade remains a core component, the company is increasingly facilitating premium game downloads on the App Store to cater to a growing audience of mobile-first players who favor genres like management sims and roguelikes.

entry.title: Elizabeth Holmes Documentary 'You Can See Everything' Explores Psychological Manipulation
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | readtheprofile.com | source | hacker news

The A24-distributed documentary *You Can See Everything*, directed by Lance Oppenheim and Nathan Fielder, follows Elizabeth Holmes in the weeks leading up to her prison sentence. Rather than a traditional true-crime retelling, the film utilizes specific cinematic techniques to manipulate the audience's emotional response and perception of Holmes in real time.

Through the strategic use of camera angles, editing, and narrative sequencing, the documentary demonstrates how easily viewers can be swayed by storytelling. The author argues that the film serves as a psychological study on how emotional impressions drive belief, forcing viewers to confront their own susceptibility to media framing.

entry.title: Creating 88x31 Animated Button Books with ImageMagick
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | k.sosnierz.me | discussion

The article provides a technical guide for creating animated 88x31 pixel GIF "buttons" that scroll through text using ImageMagick and POSIX command-line utilities. The workflow utilizes cat, tr, fold, and sed to format text into small, digestible segments, which are then converted into an animated sequence using the convert tool.

To ensure text remains legible at very low resolutions, the author recommends using specialized fonts such as TomThumb. The tutorial also includes a Python script for text centering and uses the text of Moby Dick as a practical example.

entry.title: Game Developer Podcast Discusses Misconceptions in Game Writing
entry.content:
Game Developer News | gamedeveloper.com | source

The Game Developer Podcast features Bruno Dias, Aysha Farah, and Andrea Saravia Pérez discussing common misconceptions in game writing and narrative design. Key myths addressed include the idea that screenwriting is identical to game writing, the assumption that players do not want to read, and the belief that stories are written before development begins.

The participants share professional insights from work on titles such as *Fallen London*, *Life is Strange: Double Exposure*, and *Sid Meier's Civilization VII*. The discussion highlights how these misconceptions can harm the development process and clarifies the role of narrative design within a production pipeline.
